teaching.one_liner: A severe throbbing one-sided headache preceded by a visual aura (flashing lights), with nausea and sensitivity to light/sound — the pattern since teenage years confirms this is her known migraine type, not a new concerning symptom.
differentials: Secondary headache (should be excluded if pattern changes)
red_flags: Any change in the usual aura pattern or a new type of headache — would need re-evaluation

must_ask.say: What did the flashing lights look like, and how long before the headache started?
Is the pain throbbing, one-sided, and how long has it lasted?

history.answer: I have a severe, throbbing pain on the right side of my head that started yesterday, and I've been feeling very sick to my stomach.
It built up gradually over about an hour yesterday morning rather than hitting me all at once like lightning.
The pain has been pounding continuously for the past 24 hours.
I have had similar bad headaches once or twice a month since my teenage years, and this feels like my typical attack.
The pain is strictly on the right side of my head, right behind my right eye and in my temple.
It feels like an intense, pulsating, throbbing ache, and I would rate it an eight or nine out of ten.
Moving my head, walking around, and bending over make the throbbing much worse, while resting in a pitch-black, silent room helps me tolerate it.
About thirty minutes before the pain hit, I saw shimmering, zigzag flashing lights across my vision for around twenty minutes.
I have felt very nauseous since yesterday and actually threw up twice, and any bright light or loud noise makes the pain unbearable.
No, my eye was not red or watery, my eyelid was not drooping, and my nose was not running or blocked.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, neck stiffness, or rash at all.
No, I haven't had any weakness in my arms or legs, numbness, difficulty speaking, confusion, or seizures.
No, other than the flashing lights before the headache started, I have not had blurry vision, double vision, or deep eye pain.
No, I have not hit my head or had any kind of injury recently.
I took four hundred milligrams of over-the-counter ibuprofen yesterday, but it didn't relieve the pain at all.
I only take pain pills three or four days a month when these attacks happen, so I definitely do not use them every day.
I was working late under a tight deadline and missed a lot of sleep over the past few days, which often triggers these headaches for me.
No, I do not have high blood pressure, and I do not take any blood pressure or blood-thinning pills.
No, nobody else at home has a headache, and we don't have any unvented heaters or gas appliances running.
No, I do not have a history of cancer, HIV, or any weakened immune system.
I work as a web designer, and I haven't been able to look at my screen or do any work today because the light is excruciating.
history.topic: Impact on daily life and work

history.answer: I'm pretty sure I'm having another one of my migraine attacks, just a really bad one.
I am worried about these recurring severe attacks disrupting my work and design projects if I can't get them under control.
I'm really hoping to get a prescription rescue medication that can stop the pain when ibuprofen doesn't work.
I have had these migraines since high school, but other than that I have no major medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I don't take any regular prescription medications or vitamins, only ibuprofen when I get a headache.
I have no known allergies to any medicines or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used vape products.
I only have a glass of wine on social occasions once or twice a month, and I haven't had any alcohol recently.
I work full-time as a web designer and live in an apartment with my partner.
My mother also suffered from severe migraine headaches when she was younger.
My last menstrual period started two weeks ago, my cycles are regular every 28 days, we use condoms, and there is no chance I could be pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg, pulse 76 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.6°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
The patient appears in moderate distress from pain, lying quietly with eyes shielded from the examination room light.
Pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light, extraocular movements are intact, visual fields are full, and fundoscopy demonstrates sharp optic disc margins without papilledema.
There is no tenderness over the frontal or maxillary sinuses.
Neck is supple with full range of motion; Kernig and Brudzinski signs are both negative.
Cranial nerves II through XII are grossly intact with symmetric facial movements and intact facial sensation.
Muscle strength is 5/5 in all major muscle groups across all four extremities symmetrically.
Light touch and pinprick sensation are intact and symmetric across all dermatomes without sensory deficit.
Biceps, triceps, patellar, and Achilles deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally, and plantar responses are flexor.
Finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin testing are normal, and gait is steady without ataxia.
